body: After over 5 years of using Forest, I am sadly looking elsewhere. title: From One-Time Purchase to Paywall Hell
body:
I’m beyond frustrated with what Forest has become. I bought this app as a one-time purchase years ago when it was simple, motivating, and satisfying. Back then, you could actually enjoy the full experience — growing trees, collecting plants, and feeling rewarded for staying focused.

Now? It’s subscription-based, riddled with locked content, and honestly feels like a completely different app. They love to say “everything is as it was,” but that’s simply not true.
	•	Plants and rewards that were once part of the fun are now hidden behind paywalls.
	•	Core features like whitelist mode and longer timers are restricted unless you pay extra.
	•	Updates keep breaking things — crashes, weird bugs, focus challenges not working.
	•	And worst of all, loyal users who supported the app early (and paid up front!) are left feeling ripped off.

It’s exhausting and disheartening. Instead of enhancing the experience, Forest has chipped away at what made it special. The app went from being a clever, one-time investment in productivity to a nickel-and-diming subscription trap.

I regret recommending it in the past, because the version I loved no longer exists.

title: long term user- very satisfied
body:

I’m looking forward to any developments with this the most and I love it’s still located in the forest app and not advertised as a seperate app. Very on brand. 
the full/paid version allowing the planting of trees in the subscription as well as being able to purchase with coins is one of my favourite features. 
Thank you! I hope to see updates becoming more regular for things like the focus challenge as it encourages and gamifies getting back on track. Much more so than a regular study timer.

The little reminders on the phone are super cute and I love the widgets, it leaves me with a sense of pride. 

As for suggestions I’d love to see a pause button cause usually I’ll have to get up and do something (e.g walk the dog), but I get why it isn’t available. I’d love to see a dark themed mode on the app, maybe more plants and seasonal themes. Even adding some birds or smth to make the forests feel more alive would be cute. 

Honestly just me trying to make my review sound less bot-like with the overly positive comments. 
Thank you for the app developers 🫶

title: It’s good but could be better
body:
The graphics are nice, helps to keep me focused and motivated to stay on task as the more coins I collect, the more plants I can buy.

However, it loses points for not having better features that were available in a similar free app I used before this.
I think it should have these features that the free app had:
- kills your tree (if only this was optional) if you leave the app to browse your phone
- tells you when the time will be when you finish your task
- you can input how long you want to spend on a task in total eg if it is 10h of study, you can use the app to break this 10h into chunks of time to focus

Another upgrade I would love is not available in any focus app I’ve seen but would be amazing to attach a the tasks to a calendar. That way I can organise a planner and for every task, I could use the forest timer to stay focussed and productive. I would pay a bit more for this option.

title: Great app! Heres a few suggestions
body:
Just got this app and love it! I was struggling with motivation to study and was becoming depressed. After listening to an andrew huberman podcast about dopamine I decided to do a detox from the things i was using to procrastinate. This alongside using forest has finally made study feel rewarding.  A few little recommendations,
-  i love the timeline feature and was wondering if the developers could allow us to attach photos, that would be awesome!
- also i feel that it would be much more satisfying to see your forest grow progressively instead of just adding another full grown tree. Then you would also be able to see which trees were planted first as they would be the biggest. Doing this would make it look more like a realistic forest. And the only time the trees would grow, is when ur in deep focus or using the stopwatch, further incentivising the user to focus! 

Let me know want you think, that would be great. I love this app and want to see it grow… see what i did there ;)

title: Needs in depth customisation.
body:
I’ve been using Forest for ages and have been happy with it, but I do have some feedback to the developers.

1. There has been new study research suggest the 52/17 rule (52 mins on, 17 mins off) works better for motivation, creativity and productivity. Currently Forest does not allow for that type of customisation. It would be great if we can choose specific timers instead of by 5s. 

2. Gamify the planting
With the current generation loving games, it would be perfect if we could choose where to plant the trees as that would make it look aesthetically pleasing. Additional benefit for the company as users can put a specific hashtag to tag Forest and give more influence whilst still feeling accomplished. To combat the problem of spending too much time picking where to plant the trees, give users a 20-30second timer to choose where to plant, or else the system will automatically plant trees for users. 

Hope this helps, cheers 💖

title: Good App! :-)
body:
The design and UI is very minimalist and easy to understand. It’s very motivating to be able to track your progress all in one spot and to have a physical/virtual representation of your study habits. 
Only complaint:
I wish there were more features especially for the price point. 
I love the app and supporting charity is amazing, I just wish that the interface was more engaging. It’s a study/productivity app of course, but it would be nice to have more than one way to track your progress on this app. In simple terms, this app feels very one-dimensional and only serves a single purpose. 

If you’re looking for a very clean, practical, ad-free and relatively affordable productivity tracker then this app would be great for you.
If you get bored of apps easily and want a highly engaging way to track your study habits, this app may not be the best fit for you!

title: Was great, but updates have ruined it
body:
I first downloaded this app in early 2022 and it worked exactly as advertised and did exactly what I needed. Strongly discouraged phone distractions and improved productivity. Now in the last couple of months I found I’ve been able to browse all my other apps on my phone without the usual consequences: no more notification telling me to stop, and no more withered dead tree. This defeats the purpose of having the app. There are several people on Reddit and other platforms complaining of the exact same problem! What’s the point of this app if it fails at a core feature? 
The “deep focus” mode doesn’t work, and in any case, having to mess around with Allowed Apps lists is too complicated (and according to my research, doesn’t work on iPhones anyway!) 

The updates are a failure. Give us the old version back. If not, I’ll probably delete soon, and look for something better.

title: Amazing but bug error causing my tree to wilt
body: I have only had this app for a few days after seeing lots of really good reviews from people with ADHD. I have been so excited to use it and today for the first ever time after finally beating procrastination, I think I have finally found something to not only help me focus but motivate me to actually get started studying! I study on my MacBook and use my phone for forest next to me. It was all going really well until I took a screenshot on my Mac, then the forest app closed itself after around 10 minutes of focus. I wasn’t sure why at the time so I started again, took another screenshot and the same thing happened. I’m not sure if it’s an Apple glitch with the two being linked or if it’s a forest glitch, but it was quite disheartening 😢 I don’t want to turn off the deep focus (leaving the app will cause the tree to wilt) as that keeps me motivated! Great app and I’m excited to keep using it but I hope this issue resolves!

title: Great if you have ADHD
body:
As someone with inattentive ADHD, this app is my bread and butter. I’ve tried other pomodoro apps before to limited success  but the presence of ‘gamification’ (and fact that the trees die if you use your phone really helps motivate me to use it and be more productive.

The inclusion of in app currency means that I can be ‘grinding’ for a particular tree, and that just means spending more time off my phone and getting stuff done.

It would be great if you could ‘whitelist’ certain apps (such as teams) or even set different ‘tree death’ countdowns for them (like 20 secs on Spotify so you can change playlists)

That being said, the lack of that feature is hardly a dealbreaker for what is an awesome app and I understand that this being an app (rather than a computer program or browser extension) it might not be technically possible.

All in all pretty rad

title: Planting Real Trees?
body:
The only reason why I don’t rate this app 5 stars is because, it takes a long, long time to get the 2,500 coins in order to plant a real tree. I’ve had the app for quite some time and have only planted one real tree from the app. 
And also the fact that certain ‘virtual’ trees cost 500 coins, and therefore I’d rather not buy the virtual trees because it takes so long to even get 500 coins, let alone another 2000 to plant a real tree. 
I would suggest that there be two different currencies/points, so coins go towards buying virtual trees, and diamonds or something go towards planting real trees, so that you’re able to both have the fun of having a decorative forest as well as the main reason of the app, for doing your bit to plant trees. And hopefully as well get double points for working an extra hour or something, make it more exciting and be able to earn coins easier.
Thanks

author: KyrieIrvingREAL

title: App that actually cares about you
body:
You know I was stunned when I first got this app, because:
1. It’s study function is really motivating. It feels like you’re actually slowly but surely building a forest of progress on your own instead of studying sadly away.

2. It’s addons/purchases. Instead of just ‘buying’ coins, it gives you potions where it doubles the rewards you get for your study sessions and so on. This really motivates you to study (relating to my contention that it’s an app that actually cares). Exam season is comi up, and I wouldn’t mind buying the first tier to be honest XD, even though it’s a bit superfluous. 

Though there are things that I really want to see implemented/or changed:

1. The lack of tag colours. Ugh I’m so picky, but it’s the aesthetic of the app that really brought me into this, and it’s so sad that the personalisation colour aspects are so limited. I wish they could have more colours, or shades really. 

2. The 10 minute mark minimum for planting. I understand...what’s the point of 5 minutes? What would that do? But if you’ve heard of pomodori - which is an amazingly popular study method - there’s a five minute break mark in there. I understand it’s hard, with the rewards and all, but it would be so helpful. 

3. This ones superfluous but animals. I’ve seen this request everywhere, and it would be so cool if animals could roam your forest. God...give the forest some life please. These animals could even be planted for gods sake, just please developers if you are there, animals. Please. Just this once, I don’t care about the others.

I find being able to ‘tag’ activities one of the best features, and have used that to keep track of what subjects I am studying most, and will keep an eye out to make sure I’m doing a bit of everything relatively evenly, by looking the pie chart that is automatically produced by this. 

Worth it.

body:

If you want to be more productive you should definitely get this app. It also helps with not procrastinating for example me all have those moments where we don’t want to clean our room but I found out that you can play your Spotify playlist then set a time for how long you think it is going to take you to clean your room. I love reading and this ended up helping me focus in a way that is helpful and yet entertaining for the individual. Growing plants while focusing on the task at hand makes me feel achieve as I know I am getting things done but also allowing to be planting trees and bushes to grow my tiny forest.

title: Great app!!
body:
This app helped me focus a lot more when studying. I was a bit unsure of paying money for this app, but it is completely worth it!! I used to always pick up my phone during studying to socialise or play games, but now I have no need to because Forest encourages me to stay focused! I would recommend this app to all students who need help to focus, or even just to get off your devices for a certain amount of time! I would also like to suggest two new features. Firstly, it would be nice to be able to decrease but mainly increase the time when you are using it because sometimes I do homework for longer than expected. And secondly, it would be amazing to be able to use study apps such as google classroom or restricted google use (maybe like a category based list like Apple screen time). An easy way of doing this, would be to add a way to edit a list of apps or categories you are allowed to use during the time when you are studying.

Thanks so much!

title: Awesome but...
body: Forest is definitely not a waste of money. It encourages you to sit down and stay focused by growing beautiful virtual trees that can earn you enough coins to grow an actual tree! How cool is that! My problem is though, there’s some sort of bug where whenever I click on the ‘Real Forest’ section, the app clashes and my phone exits from the app. This prohibits me from accessing the feature of growing a real tree which is really disappointing since I’ve been gathering coins to do so. Also, another suggestion is to have the opportunity to purchase lofi music as the sounds, as a lot of people listen to that when they study and if you’re in deep focus mode, you can’t go on another app like YouTube to play it. Someone here on the reviews also mentioned having a more definite sound for the end of the productivity sessions which I completely agree with. It can also be like a couple vibrations. It’s an awesome app with an amazing concept but it would be even better if the bugs are removed and the above suggestions are taken into consideration. It would be great to have a feedback section on the app to easily point out some more improvements that can be made.

body: I’ve sadly had to change my rating. This app WAS amazing, so helpful at keeping me focused for uni study and not looking at social media. However, NOW it’s basically useless. They have updated the app so that now, when you exit the app, nothing happens. Your tree doesn’t die, you can use whatever other apps you want. They say it wasn’t working on iOS, yet I never had an issue before. Now, you need to turn on “deep focus” mode in order for it to work as it did before. This requires a passcode (no idea why you’d need that) so if you don’t want one or can’t use one (which I can not), too bad. Totally changed the app, no longer what was signed up for.

title: Surprisingly effective
body: I didn’t think it was worth an actual app just to tell me to split up my study time into easy blocks, but I decided to give it a go after reading the reviews. It definitely reminds me to stay focused and not get distracted by a notification or a random thought leading to a loss of time accidentally scrolling through social media or messaging friends. The only thing I would change is to have a more clear notification for the end of each session. I can get too involved in lectures or videos which means I’m not using the music provided & I never notice when the time is up. I end up going too far over time and feel a bit like a zombie/consume too much content and it’s a bit of a wasted session. If it could flash on and vibrate to notify me of the end of the time, that would give it 5/5 from me.

title: Really helpful, still require self discipline
body:
So I’ve been using this app for quite a while now since it was recommended at a study skills talk at my school. I downloaded it immediately, and since then I’ve found it extremely helpful when I’m trying to knuckle down and get things done. It really gives you the incentive to work for the entire duration of the timer, and then you get a nice pay off afterwards.

The only thing to note is that you need to have the discipline and drive to actually use it, and use it to its full potential. You may be tempted to just not set the timer and trust yourself, or you might want to have a quick look at something and so you let your tree die.

Otherwise, wonderful app, perfect for students who struggle with procrastination and distractions (such as myself).

title: Intriguingly calming
body:
A very simplistically artistic application. It helps with distraction as it makes you almost feel bad that you don’t let your tree grow. I also love the idea that taking a break from your phone, regardless the intent, can be used to help regrow trees. 

The group function of this app is also very helpful as it increases the amount of trees grown and it also promotes distraction free group activities such as study. Study is in my opinion the best use for this app as I sit down knowing I am doing something good for myself, the environment and my phone battery :) 

I also love how much more control it’s given me when it comes to impulsively opening snaps or messages from colleagues, now I just let the notifications roll in and feel really good about it.

title: Really good! Some suggestions though:
body:
First thing out of the way, this a very good app if you struggle with motivation and distraction to help you stay focussed for short or long bursts of time. Is worth the 3 bucks. However, some features I believe would improve the experience are: 

- a way to pause the timer if you need to exit the app for something that doesn’t kill the tree. I guess you could see this as cheating but if you cheat then you’re only really cheating yourself so... This would be extremely helpful for that moment when you’re working on an assignment and suddenly realise that you need the photos you took on your phone which means you can’t continue working on it without killing the tree

- cheaper trees or greater rewards. It takes a ridiculous amount of time to reach 500 coins and hence kind of takes away the incentive to work towards earning them.

Thanks for reading! Hopefully this was helpful

title: Amazing app and so helpful!
body:
This app is so simple but amazing. It helps me all the time to stay off my phone for a certain task and stay focused in the moment, and I’m motivated by the fact that if I succeed I’ll have a beautiful tree to add to a lovely forest and I don’t want to kill a tree. It’s a great visual for the time I’ve focussed.
Also this app is amazing because after a certain amount of time focussed and coins made (I think it’s 5000?), trees are planted in real life! The people behind this app seem so lovely and like they care about both the individual using the app, and the greater picture for human well-being and the environment.

body: My kids (6 and 7 y.o) saw me creating my own forest and became very curious about the app. I let them to play around a bit and they got very excited about the whole idea. "Morning routine" etc If the kids start getting distracted I warn them that will have to "cancel" (kill) the growing tree.  That keeps them very motivated. Less time In front of TV and more time for outdoor play, reading, piano. Also we added each other to friends and can see our trees growing, do one task together. Very happy to find a way to motivate girls and make them focus on a task!

title: Love the iPhone app but the watch app isn't working
body:
When I open the watch app (watch series 3 and iPhone xs with all latest updates) you see the Forest grid and when I tap on that it just says "start planting today!".  But there's no way to start planting on the watch app (without going to the phone to start). Which kind of makes the watch app of minimal if any use if you have to have the phone right there to start it? The whole point of the series 3 and 4 Apple watches is that they can be used independently of the phone. 

If I'm getting it wrong or misunderstanding how it works then I'm happy to change the review. Otherwise maybe replace "start planting today" with "open the app on your phone to start planting"?

One tip if possible for the phone app is to allow a whitelist of apps. One of the tasks I do is reading and use Kindle on my phone for that. However the app kills the tree everytime I do that task. However I understand if the limitations of ios means that you can't whitelist.

I’m a lot less likely to stick with using this app if the quickest way to setup the study environment I desire (tree and sounds I want) involves paying over and over for elixir only to have the silly price increase after each purchase! title: Definitely worth it
body: This app is definitely worth the money! I was a bit hesitant when I first saw it, and I thought it seemed counterintuitive, but it is so useful for studying- I don't know what I'd do without it. Once you set a timer, you can't leave the app or the tree will die, meaning that you're less likely to go on social media or games to procrastinate. Knowing that you have a timer also makes you want to stay focused rather than zoning out, and there is a sense of pride when you see how long you've managed to stay focused for. I managed to study for about three hours on one of the days and didn't feel emotionally or mentally drained because of the ability to set a rest-time timer. I really liked the rest timer because it doesn't let you add more time on once it's up so you can't be tempted to say "just five minutes more" and then not get back to work. When I wasn't using the app, I would procrastinate for hours and relax when I needed to study, but as soon as it was on I got heaps done. I really recommend the app.

title: It’s counterintuitive, but it works
body: I was a bit sceptical about using an app to wean me off IT - but Forest’s main message (‘Stay focussed’) is what it really delivers on. Like having a personal trainer at the gym, it gently encourages you to stay with a sustained task (reading, writing, editing, whatever) without giving in too soon. ‘Just four more minutes ... just three more minutes.’ The app started me at 25 minutes and I’m now stretching that to longer periods of sustained focus (like adding more weights to a familiar routine at the gym). The tree-planting reward? A bit goofy, but at least it’s a fun way to show yourself how many sustained sessions you’ve achieved in a day. The other stats are helpful little rewards too.

title: Time Hack Severely Undermines Amazing App
body:
This is a really great app with awesome design, the best on the market by far. However, there is a killer bug where you can go into iPhone Settings, move forward the system time and grow the tree. Now this wouldn't have been such an awful thing if there is no reward system. However because you can use the coins to unlock new trees and even the ultimate "planting a real tree", this exploit really diminishes one's motivation to work towards these goals. It also makes you wonder how many people on the leaderboard are legitimate.

Overall, this bug kills the mechanism on which such a great app runs. Please fix it.

title: Put down your phone and experience life!
body:
I find it *so* hard to not constantly check my phone while I'm doing other things; it's distracting and I never put my full attention into any one task at a time.

Now, when I set my Forest timer, I'm growing a tree or a flower or something else beautiful for my garden, so I feel like I mustn't disturb my phone while that is happening.

It helps with work, obviously, but it also helps with things like paying full attention to a tv show I like - I'm not constantly looking up from my phone, saying, 'hang on, what did she just do?' and having to rewind, only to miss the same bit again because I've gone straight back to my phone.

It also helps with socialising and spending time with loved ones. If it's family dinner, I can set my phone for two hours and grow a tree and be much more engaged with the conversation around me. Same with friends - brunch, set my forest for 45 minutes and actually pay attention to what's going on in my friends' lives.

My little sister uses Forest to help her focus on writing her Masters thesis. Two-hour blocks of not touching her phone, and she knocks out twelve pages of writing.

I think if I wanted to go back to writing my novel, Forest would be a useful tool. Don't get distracted by phonecalls and SMS, Facebook, videogames, emails, and Pokemon!

It's such a simple idea, and it works so well. I have traits of OCD and my phone is always at hand, with pages to read and friends to catch up with and game achievements to get... Forest is like a 'calm down' button. The world won't end if you put your phone down for half an hour and focus on other things.

It's a great tool for mindfulness - being aware of the present moment and experiencing things fully without unhelpful distractions.

Anyway, I like it. Thanks, devs.
